extracted.intended_audience: computer vision / machine learning researchers and practitioners working on character image animation
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating methods that animate a reference character image given a driving/target pose sequence, with emphasis on generalizing across varied character types (including anthropomorphic characters) and improving motion representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality video generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Generates high-quality videos from a reference image and target pose sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The core goal is perceptually and temporally coherent video output given a single reference image and a driving/target pose sequence; evaluation should assess visual fidelity, artifact absence, and frame-to-frame consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality across character types (including anthropomorphic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicability to various character types (collectively named X), not limited to human figures; generalizes to anthropomorphic characters commonly used in industries like gaming and entertainment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods should be tested on diverse character designs and not rely on assumptions specific to human anatomy; benchmarks/datasets should include non-human and stylized characters to measure generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced motion representation (Pose Indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce a Pose Indicator which captures comprehensive motion pattern from the driving video through both implicit and explicit manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should verify that the motion representation encodes both overall movement patterns and finer temporal relations; ablations should compare models with and without the Pose Indicator to quantify improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit motion capture via CLIP visual features
rubrics_metrics.description: The implicit component leverages CLIP visual features of a driving video to extract its gist of motion, like the overall movement pattern and temporal relations among motions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether using global/semantic visual features (e.g., CLIP) improves the model's ability to capture high-level motion gist and temporal structure; experiments may compare different feature backbones and measure robustness to varied driving videos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit motion simulation to strengthen generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: The explicit component strengthens the generalization of LDM by simulating possible inputs in advance that may arise during inference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training-time simulation of varied/perturbed inputs should be used to improve inference robustness; evaluation should include out-of-distribution driving motions and input corruptions to measure resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rigid pose imposition — comprehend movement pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods should not rigidly impose the pose sequence onto the target character; instead they must comprehend and adapt to the driving video's movement pattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics and qualitative analysis should check for naturalistic motion transfer (e.g., plausible articulation, preservation of character identity) rather than simple framewise pose transplantation that yields unnatural deformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal coherence and relation modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Capture temporal relations among motions to produce coherent sequences (not just per-frame pose matching).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate temporal metrics (e.g., motion continuity, temporal FID, optical-flow based consistency) and include qualitative sequences to judge whether motion dynamics and rhythm are preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Latent Diffusion Models (LDM) and their generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage LDMs as the generative backbone and ensure they generalize across character types when provided enhanced motion cues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how LDM architectures perform with/without motion indicators, and measure sample quality, diversity, and fidelity; consider computational/training trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarking on Animated Anthropomorphic Benchmark (A^2Bench)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce and use A^2Bench to evaluate performance on universal and widely applicable animation images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use A^2Bench to compare methods across standardized splits and metrics, ensuring benchmarks include diverse anthropomorphic characters and representative driving motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical superiority demonstrated through extensive experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate the proposed method's superiority and effectiveness compared to state-of-the-art methods via extensive experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative evaluation should include quantitative metrics (e.g., FID, LPIPS, user studies) and qualitative examples; ablation studies should isolate contributions (Pose Indicator implicit vs explicit) and report statistical significance where appropriate.
